description: Agent Inventory: submit an inventory valuation with the counts and purchase records it answers to: the valuation with its reference, the day it is as of, the first day of the period, currency, the total value stated and each line with its id, the item, ownership (owned or consigned), units valued, unit cost, value, the day the cost was set, the purchase record the cost comes from and any note; the counted quantities with each item and units counted; the purchase records with each reference, item, day and unit cost paid; optionally the consigned stock held with each item, consignor and units. The signed report gives the valuation, each item’s units valued against the units counted, each unit cost against the purchase record it comes from, each cost set before the period against the purchases inside it, and each line against the consigned stock held for others, and counts them, and names a divergent valuation: quantities valued above the counted quantity, unit costs that drift from the purchase record with no note, stale unit costs carried across periods, and consigned stock valued as owned; then line values or a total that do not recompute and items valued with no count, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No valuation lines, no counted quantities, no purchase record answering to a line, no period start or cost dates, or no ownership stated leaves those points unverified. A unit cost answers to the purchase it cites, or else to the latest purchase of the item on or before the day its cost was set, or the valuation date, and a note on a line explains its cost; items match by their SKU or their words, units compare to the hundredth, amounts to the cent and dates by the day. This reads the stock valuation itself, line by line against counts and purchases: wever_bookkeeping-ledger-check reads the ledger postings the valuation feeds, while the inventory valuation check reads the quantities, unit costs and ownership behind the stock value before it is posted. Verdict inventory_valuation_divergent, inventory_valuation_partial, inventory_valuation_unverified or inventory_valuation_consistent. POST /api/inventory-valuation-check. Reads the inventory records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads the records as supplied only: it never moves stock, never places or cancels an order, never writes to anyone’s inventory system and never adjusts a record, which stay with the business and its staff, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Inventory reads inventory records: a stock count, receiving records, shrinkage and loss records, a stock adjustment log, an inventory valuation, reorder records, a dead stock record and consignment stock records, each against the system stock record, the purchase or consignment orders, the count and sales records, the count and the period close, the counts and purchase records, the stock levels and lead times, the movement window and period report, or the sale and settlement records it answers to. The family checks whether the stock record can be trusted; the Agent Bookkeeping family reads the ledger the stock feeds, and the boutique tools act on one store’s orders. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-inventory-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-inventory/.
